texts.name: waiting / leaving
texts.text: Every evening, he waited at the window. Across the city, she was already leaving.

texts.name: the house
texts.text: I returned to the house. Nothing had moved. But everything was gone.

texts.name: the harbor
texts.text: He walked down to the harbor. The ships were leaving. He could not leave. He remembered his mother at the door.

pairs.a: Every evening, he waited at the window. Across the city, she was already leaving.
pairs.b: Once, he waited at the window. Across the city, she was already leaving.
pairs.expect: a: the window comes back (REPEAT); b: it does not

pairs.a: He waited at the window while she left the house.
pairs.b: He waited at the window after she left the house.
pairs.expect: a: the strands alternate (A B A); b: the earlier strand closes, no cut back

pairs.a: He walked to the door. He leaves the house.
pairs.b: He walked to the door. He cannot leave the house.
pairs.expect: a: a departure on screen (COMPLETE); b: the lead-up held, never completed (SUSPEND)

pairs.a: I returned to the house. Nothing had moved. But everything was gone.
pairs.b: I returned to the house. Nothing had moved. Everything was still there.
pairs.expect: a: the same shot or the same place emptied carries the turn; b: a plain continuation

pairs.a: She walked to the station. She left.
pairs.b: She walked to the station. She never left.
